answer: State-marked identity tokens. Each agent gets a private signing token whose output is blended with a slow-diffusing pigment tied to prior state, so a clone of one agent's token yields mismatched marks. Every message carries a marble-like serial impression derived from that state; duplicates produce visibly divergent patterns. A quill-signed audit log records impressions. To pass, an attacker must run each duplicate as a genuinely independent state lineage, costing days of serialized recomputation plus separate audit histories per identity.
